notes: Commercial parol lease of land to liquor dealers for bottling/storage business (tenancy at will) and eminent-domain condemnation by a railroad; no dwelling, lodging, or boarding-house occupancy at issue.
Dispute between commercial landlord and business tenants over removal of trade fixtures at lease renewal; no residential letting or lodging/boarding issue.
Easement/right-of-way dispute over an alley and a theater fire escape; no compensated occupancy of a dwelling at issue.

Will-construction dispute over which relative has first option to occupy the testator's house for an indefinite/life term at a nominal fixed rental plus carrying charges; a testamentary family arrangement, not a market letting of rooms/lodging and not short-term.
Dispute between a mortgagee-purchaser and a lessee over ownership of an amusement-park scenic railway as a trade fixture; no dwelling/lodging occupancy.
Dispute over possession of a public market stall held under a municipal license; commercial vendor space, not a dwelling or lodging arrangement.
Deed construction of an easement/right to build over an alley; no occupancy-for-pay issue.
Commercial lease forfeiture-for-nonpayment procedure (place of rent demand); tenant is a business (A. G. Spalding & Bros.), not a residential lodger/boarder.

Foreign-attachment jurisdiction turning on the meaning of 'residence' vs. 'domicil' for an ambassador; discusses residence generally but not compensated occupancy of another's dwelling or lodging/boarding practice.
Constitutional challenge to the state moving-picture censorship statute as an exercise of the police power; unrelated to lodging or dwelling occupancy.

Landlord-tenant dispute over rent-acceleration and distress on an assigned commercial lease of an entire hotel (Hotel Vannear) to a business operator; the case addresses lease-assignment/rent covenants only and does not discuss the character or regulation of guest occupancy within the hotel, so it is only a passing mention of a hotel.

holding_summary: A deed restriction limiting land use to a 'private dwelling house' is violated by an apartment house with a common entrance, hall, and stairway, because the word 'private' excludes buildings used for residential purposes of a public character, such as hotels and general public boarding or apartment houses, as distinguished from a building for the sole and exclusive occupancy of one family.

quotes.text: there is a well defined difference between an apartment house, operated by the owner for profit through leasing different stories or suites of rooms, and a dwelling intended and calculated to be for the sole and exclusive occupancy of one family, suitably constructed for that purpose.
The word “private” further restricts the buildings by excluding all such as are used for residential purposes of a public character, like hotels and general public boarding or apartment houses.
The restriction in this deed prohibits the erection of an apartment house.

notes: Restrictive-covenant case classifying multi-family/boarding rental buildings as distinct from and excluded from 'private dwelling' use; relevant to the doctrinal line between ordinary household occupancy and public/commercial letting, though the letting here is by a commercial owner-operator, not a householder.

Constitutional zoning case striking down a building set-back-line ordinance as an unreasonable exercise of the police power; concerns yard/setback space, not the letting or regulation of lodging/boarding occupancy.

holding_summary: Construing a deed restriction that permitted 'houses' but barred use as a 'hotel or tavern' or for any purpose 'offensive' to neighboring owners, the court held an apartment house is not a hotel and is not barred: a hotel is a building held out to the public where transient persons are received and entertained as guests for compensation, whereas an apartment house is a dwelling for several families, each living separate and apart, occupied under long-term leases, and its erection was therefore permitted.

quotes.text: A hotel is a building held out to the public as a place where all transient persons who come will be received and entertained as guests for compensation, 32 C. J. 527.
an apartment house is not a hotel, but is a building used as a dwelling for several families, each living separate and apart.

We hold the language “a building for any other purpose offensive to the owners or occupiers of other properties” is not sufficiently clear, explicit or definite in use or reference to restrict the use permitted under clause “(a)” on the word “houses” which concedes the right to erect an apartment house.

notes: Favors treating multi-family rental housing as an ordinary, non-offensive use distinct from transient innkeeping, while simultaneously drawing a sharp adverse-leaning line that hotel/innkeeping-for-transients is a different, prohibitable category; marked mixed for that reason. Letting here is long-term apartment tenancy by a commercial building owner, not short-term householder lodging.
Zoning appeal over a garage set-back permit under the Pittsburgh zoning ordinance; no lodging or boarding-house issue.
Commercial store/basement lease dispute over rights to an outer wall and sidewalk for a lunch stand; no residential lodging or boarding occupancy.
